strengths: Demonstrates practical value of cascaded pretrained models achieving competitive performance without dataset-specific fine-tuning, addressing a real problem in TQA deployment
Strong robustness under query paraphrasing (Table 2): CRAFT maintains 0.04 point drop vs. DTR's 8.38+ point degradation, suggesting better generalization
Comprehensive stage-wise ablations showing clear incremental gains and transparent methodology
Well-written with clear figures and attention to practical deployment considerations (token consumption analysis showing 70% reduction)
Competitive retrieval results on NQ-Tables: R@1=41.13, R@10=87.16, R@50=96.84, matching or exceeding THYME in several metrics
weaknesses: Critical missing ablation: No evaluation of CRAFT's retrieval performance without Gemini-generated descriptions and sub-questions. Combined impact of these preprocessing components on the three-stage pipeline is unknown, making it unclear whether improvements come from cascading or preprocessing

Unfair baseline comparison: CRAFT uses Gemini-enriched data while trained baselines (THYME, SSDR) were trained on raw data. Baselines not given access to same preprocessing, violating fair comparison principles

Severely limited evaluation scope: Only NQ-Tables dataset (919 unique test queries). No evaluation on WikiTableQuestions, Spider, or other TQA benchmarks. Claims about 'adaptability to evolving domains' are unsupported

Reproducibility severely compromised by dependence on proprietary APIs (Gemini Flash 1.5, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) with no code release mentioned. Future reference ('Team et al., 2025') for Gemini raises concerns

Inconsistent end-to-end results undermine reliability claims: CRAFT underperforms in several settings (e.g., n=1 Qwen: 33.33 vs THYME 37.28); few-shot results (Table 12) highly unstable with no clear patterns
Misleading terminology: 'Training-free' is inaccurate—models are trained elsewhere; more precisely NQ-Tables fine-tuning free. Generalizability claims exceed evidence
Missing computational analysis: No actual timing comparisons despite mentioning performance-runtime tradeoff. Preprocessing costs (Gemini API calls for 169,898 tables) not discussed
No statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or analysis of high variability in few-shot results across 919 test queries
Arbitrary design choices lack justification: Filtering thresholds (5000→1000→100), mini-table row count (5), and threshold selection process unexplained

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablation studies, robustness testing via query paraphrasing, and end-to-end evaluation across multiple LLMs
Strong practical contributions: 33× reduction in embedding calls and 70% reduction in context length through mini-tables and cascaded filtering without sacrificing accuracy
Mini-table design effectively reduces noise in downstream QA; convincing case studies (Tables 16-17) demonstrate benefits even when gold tables are retrieved at moderate ranks
Thorough robustness analysis showing near-perfect recovery under query paraphrasing (0.04% drop vs. 6-12% for DTR), demonstrating superior generalization vs. fine-tuned methods
Detailed error analysis with qualitative case studies providing insights into failure modes and when intermediate representations improve reasoning
Reproducibility: clear implementation details, prompts in appendix, code promised, transparent hyperparameter reporting
weaknesses: Misleading 'training-free' framing: all components use pre-trained models from massive datasets (Gemini, OpenAI text-embedding-3, Sentence Transformer); more accurately 'dataset-specific fine-tuning free' rather than truly training-free

Limited technical novelty: cascaded retrieval is well-established (Wang et al. 2011; Glass et al. 2022); core contribution is engineering integration of existing techniques; mini-tables are simple row filtering; no principled justification for architectural choices (stage cutoffs at 5000/100 appear arbitrary)

Overstated claims on OTT-QA: paper emphasizes 'competitive results' at higher recalls, but R@1 gap vs. THYME is substantial (55.56 vs. 66.67, 11.1 points); end-to-end evaluation uses oracle setup with gold passages (not true open-retrieval), significantly weakening claims

Unfair comparison concerns: text-embedding-3-large (Stage 3) is a recent proprietary model newer than most baselines; unclear whether NQ-Tables SOTA improvement comes from the method vs. superior embeddings; missing ablation using earlier embedding models

Critical dependence on proprietary services: Gemini Flash 1.5 for descriptions/decomposition, OpenAI embeddings create reproducibility risks; cost implications not discussed; contradicts 'lightweight plug-and-play' positioning

Insufficient design justification: why different models for Stage 2 vs. Stage 3? How sensitive to mini-table row count (5 rows)? Limited exploration of alternative cascade configurations; preprocessing row ranking via Sentence Transformer adds non-trivial computation

Robustness evaluation limited to single paraphrasing approach and DTR baseline; few-shot results (Table 14) show high variance without statistical significance testing; no multiple runs or error bars; only single-hop and oracle multi-hop evaluation
